predictions.claim: The parametric model checks with term size per law at most 1.5x the M1 model's on the same fixture laws. Operationalized on fixture milestone T12 (toy machine tests_m2/fixtures/oracles/, parameters agg and dec from its oracle sidecar): the generated model passes bend; the model is parametric (L_orc_agg_value, true of the agg stand-in, is REFUTED by a witness other than the stand-in); the four parameter laws are decided as the fixtures predict (3 PROVED, 1 REFUTED) with BendTT verdict checked; and for each fixture law PROVED in both encodings (L_orc_cf_commit, L_orc_runs_ok, L_orc_run_post, L_orc_dec_pad), term size (characters of the BendTT kernel entries in the law's kernel cone over its model, plus its emitted LAWS.bend without comment lines) is at most 1.5x that of the same law in its M1 form (parameter binders and CF/hypothesis premises removed, claim kept) on the M1 model of the same machine (tests_m2/fixtures/oracles_standin/: byte-identical facts, each oracle compiled in as a target-library stand-in builtin), run as the same milestone.

A fixture oracle with two hypothesis variants yields a law pair with different statuses, reported as a split: the oracle dec with variants HypD-pad and HypD-exact (family HypD) gives L_orc_dec_pad PROVED and L_orc_dec_exact REFUTED (BendTT verdict checked), and splits.json reports the pair on family HypD with split true.

The agg inhabitant of CF(h, S) checks: the premise CF(agg, {[1], [2]}) of L_orc_cf_commit (PROVED) is inhabited with agg := the oracle record's concrete instance (AGG_BASE + enc(xs)), recorded as {"instance": "agg"}; the inhabitant states the law's premise and re-checks under bend; and with an agg instance that violates the premise (a constant) no inhabitant claims the instance.
